title: Integration test harness: containerised full-workflow test gated on release candidate
description: There is no automated end-to-end test that validates a new moeb binary exercises the complete pipeline correctly. After a release candidate is built, a containerised environment should: (1) run `moeb init` from scratch, (2) inject a known set of canary signals, (3) trigger the full fix-signal → spec → run → candidate-tag flow via the conductor, (4) assert that the canary signals are resolved and no new signals re-report the same missing capability. This closes the feedback loop on whether an implementation actually works in a live moeb instance. Claude Haiku should be used as the AI provider to limit test cost. The container should be deployed and exercised as a GitHub Actions job triggered on candidate tag creation.
proposed_resolution: 1. Define a canonical set of cheap canary signals (e.g. add a field to a config struct, add a CHANGELOG entry) that exercise the pipeline without requiring complex implementation. 2. Build a Docker image containing the moeb binary, canary signal seed, and a conductor instance. 3. Write a GitHub Actions workflow triggered on candidate tag push that: launches the container, runs the full pipeline via conductor with Haiku, reads signal statuses on exit, fails the job if any canary signal remains unresolved or a new signal re-reports the tested capability. 4. Report pass/fail and token cost back to the candidate PR as a comment.
gating_condition: Requires conductor to be operational (Ouro project signal b0000005).
